description: When soldiers of World War I traveled to Europe to fight, they would bring real animals meant to lift their spirits. One of them was an orphaned black bear from Canada. Tina Kraus explains how the cub inspired Winnie the Pooh, now 100 years old.
title: The real story behind Winnie the Pooh, born in the shadow of WWI

description: Republicans have dominated elections in Great Plains states for a generation. But with the midterms fast approaching, Ed O'Keefe reports that some voters in Iowa now say they're considering all of their options.
title: As high diesel prices hit Great Plains, some considering all options in midterms

description: Tensions flared in the Middle East following attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia. Leigh Kiniry reports.

description: President Trump announced that he struck an energy ceasefire with Ukraine and Russia. Hours later, the Russians hit a neighborhood in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv, including a power plant. It follows new criticism for the president's diesel deal with Russia. Taurean Small reports from the White House.
title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, Russia later strikes Ukraine

description: Pope Leo XIV, 71, said he will have surgery this week to remove a nodule in his lung. Chris Livesay has the latest in Rome.

description: Tropical Storm Rachel caused devastation along the waterfront in Long Beach, California. Akiko Fujita reports and Grant Gilmore has the forecast.

description: The first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season roared into Florida late Friday, unleashing destructive winds, extensive flooding and spinning up tornadoes across the Southeast. Jason Allen reports on the damage.

title: Billy Crystal on finding humor in the darkest of times

description: In this web exclusive, comedian Billy Crystal talks with correspondent Tracy Smith about the inspiration behind his new one-man Broadway show, "860": his family's home that was destroyed in last year's Pacific Palisades wildfire.
title: Extended interview: Billy Crystal

description: In January 2025, a wildfire burned more than 5,000 homes in the Pacific Palisades neighborhood of Los Angeles, including the home of Billy Crystal. The fire took everything, but in the smoldering ruins of what was once his family home, Crystal found inspiration for his latest one-man stage show, "860." Crystal talks with correspondent Tracy Smith about bringing the story of his home to Broadway, sharing what he lost, and what he learned.
title: Billy Crystal on finding humor in the darkest of times

description: In this extended conversation, political strategist and podcaster Steve Bannon talks with "Sunday Morning" senior contributor Ted Koppel about populist and nationalist politics in the U.S. and abroad; the ground game of Democratic Socialists and prospects for the 2026 midterms; Trumpism and election denialism; and media coverage of politics.
title: Extended interview: Steve Bannon

description: Christine Quaiff has captured dozens of lost dogs for grateful owners around Richmond, Virginia. Her most recent case was a desperate search for two Goldendoodles, Bailee and Tobey, who escaped from Annie Olup's car after she was in a near-fatal accident. Steve Hartman reports on how one tenacious searcher helped enable a tearful reunion.
title: The dog rescuer

description: Clint Hill was a secret service agent who was on the scene the day President John F. Kennedy was assassinated. In pictures splashed across newspapers, it was Hill who was seen climbing atop the presidential limousine to push First Lady Jackie Kennedy out of the way to protect her life. In 1975, he spoke with 60 Minutes correspondent Mike Wallace.v
title: Secret Service Agent Number 9 Clint Hill | 60 Minutes Archive

description: A key figure in President Trump's 2016 campaign and a former White House adviser, Steve Bannon remains an outspoken champion of the MAGA movement and has courted far-right parties in Europe. He talks with "Sunday Morning" senior contributor Ted Koppel about Trump's place in history; the influence of Nazi propaganda filmmaker Leni Riefenstahl on his productions; and why he believes a Republican victory in the midterms is imperative.
title: Steve Bannon on the GOP and the midterms: "We can't afford to lose"

title: Noah Kahan: Songs of sorrow and joy

description: In this extended conversation, Luke Burbank talks with singer-songwriter Noah Kahan about how his home state of Vermont has inspired his music; dealing with stardom; the process of writing his latest album, "The Great Divide"; and founding his mental health non-profit, The Busybody Project.
title: Extended interview: Noah Kahan

description: The song "Stick Season," which Noah Kahan posted on TikTok in 2020, propelled the singer-songwriter from Vermont into a multi-platinum, two-time Grammy-nominated artist, with sold-out stadium shows. Now, his fourth album, "The Great Divide," with lyrics that describe friendships lost, family divisions, and bouts of depression and anxiety, has topped the Billboard chart. Kahan talks with correspondent Luke Burbank about battling for mental health, and why he's now looking forward to accessing joy in his music.
title: Noah Kahan: Songs of sorrow and joy

title: The return of the Gruffalo

description: In 1999, children's book author Julia Donaldson created a monster: "The Gruffalo," an award-winning story about a mouse who conjures a terrifying beast. With illustrations by Axel Scheffler, the book was a runaway bestseller. Now, the pair has released their third book in the series, "Gruffalo Granny," which has become the U.K.'s bestselling book of the year (of any genre), and the fastest-selling picture book ever. They talk with correspondent Elizabeth Palmer about their creative partnership, and about books that address big ideas for small people.
title: The return of the Gruffalo

description: In her new book, "Ethel Kennedy: The Extraordinary Life and Bold Legacy," daughter Kerry Kennedy writes about a woman who maintained positivity and resilience despite public and private tragedies. She also discusses the dichotomy of Ethel's relationship with her son, Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
title: The extraordinary joy of Ethel Kennedy
